question: Which of the following particles contribute to the mass number?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Protons and Neutrons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **mass number** (denoted by the symbol **A**) of an atom is defined as the total number of **protons** and **neutrons** present in the **nucleus** of an atom. Together, these two types of particles are known as **nucleons** because they reside in the atomic nucleus. *Hence, statement D is correct.*
 
• **Protons** are subatomic particles with a **positive electric charge** of **+1e**. While they contribute significantly to the mass, they do not constitute the mass number alone as neutrons are also present in almost all nuclei (except common Hydrogen). *Hence, statement B is incorrect.*
 
• **Neutrons** are subatomic particles with **no net electric charge** and a mass slightly greater than that of a proton. They were discovered by **James Chadwick** in **1932**.
 
• **Electrons** are negatively charged particles that orbit the nucleus. The mass of an electron is approximately **9.109 × 10&sup{-31} kg**, which is about **1/1836** of the mass of a proton. Due to this extremely small value, electron mass is considered **negligible** when calculating the **mass number**. *Hence, statements A and C are incorrect.*
 
• The **mass number** is always a **whole number** because it is a count of discrete particles (protons and neutrons).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Atomic Number (Z):**

 
 
• This refers to the number of **protons** in the nucleus of an atom. It determines the **chemical identity** of the element. For a neutral atom, the atomic number also equals the number of **electrons**.
 
 
 
• **Isotopes:**
 
 
• These are atoms of the same element that have the same **atomic number** but different **mass numbers**. This occurs because they have the same number of **protons** but a different number of **neutrons**.
 
• An example is **Carbon-12** (6 protons, 6 neutrons) and **Carbon-14** (6 protons, 8 neutrons), used in **radiocarbon dating**.
 
 
 
• **Isobars:**
 
 
• These are atoms of different chemical elements that have the same **mass number** but different **atomic numbers**. An example is **Argon-40** and **Calcium-40**.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Mass vs. Mass Number:**
 
 
• While the mass number is a count of nucleons, **atomic mass** is the weighted average mass of an element's naturally occurring isotopes, usually expressed in **Atomic Mass Units (amu)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mathematical Formula:** The relationship is expressed as **A = Z + N**, where **A** is the mass number, **Z** is the atomic number (protons), and **N** is the **neutron number**.
 
• **Notation:** In chemical notation, the mass number is written as a **superscript** to the left of the element symbol, while the atomic number is written as a **subscript**. For example, in **²³⁵₉₂U**, 235 is the mass number and 92 is the atomic number.
 
• **Discovery Facts:** The nucleus was discovered by **Ernest Rutherford** through the **Gold Foil Experiment** in **1911**, which proved that most of an atom's mass is concentrated in a tiny, dense center.
 
• **Stability:** The ratio of **neutrons to protons (N/Z ratio)** is a key factor in determining the **nuclear stability** of an atom. Elements with high atomic numbers require more neutrons to overcome the electrostatic repulsion between protons.
